title: PPG Product Wiring — Machine-Capable Post Processor Generation That Actually Works
source: User: generate a perfect working post processor for user's desired machine, controller, features. Audit revealed: 38-stage pipeline EXISTS but PPG UI calls lightweight template generator instead. All engines exist. Wiring is missing.
description: Wire the existing 38-stage PostProcessorPipelineEngine into the PPG UI so users get REAL physics-optimized G-code when they click Generate Post. Machine fingerprinting drives pipeline stage selection. Controller dialect drives output formatting. Feature toggles map to pipeline StageConfig flags. The post library becomes a launcher into the real pipeline, not a static template. Result: user selects Haas VF-2SS → gets production-ready G-code with HSM G187, TSC M88/M89, probing macros, physics-optimized S/F per block, Kienzle force-limited feeds, chatter-aware RPM — all formatted in Haas NGC dialect.

engines_that_already_exist: PostProcessorPipelineEngine.ts (4,800 lines) — 38 stages, COMPLETE, produces real optimized G-code
ControllerDialectEngine.ts (1,348 lines) — 25 dialects with syntax, canned cycles, probing, features
AdvancedPostProcessorEngine.ts (986 lines) — HSM, adaptive clearing, RTCP, tool management
PostSelectionEngine.ts (596 lines) — auto-selects features per job context
SpeedFeedOrchestratorEngine.ts (2,851 lines) — 8 resolvers + Monte Carlo UQ
ThermalWearCouplingEngine.ts (542 lines) — coupled Usui RK4 ODE (Stage 2.7b)
ProductEngine.ts — ppg_generate, ppg_validate, ppg_compare (8 working actions)
ui_that_already_exists: PostProcessorGeneratorPage.tsx (2,787 lines) — full UI with 5 lanes, file I/O, diff viewer, history
MachinePickerPanel.tsx — machine fingerprinting (manufacturer + model → controller + features)
routes_that_exist: /ppg/generate → prism_cam post_process — THIS is the pipeline entry point that exists but UI doesn't use
the_critical_disconnect: PPG UI 'Generate Post' → calls /ppg/template → ProductEngine.ppg_generate → returns TEMPLATE
SHOULD call → /ppg/generate → prism_cam post_process → PostProcessorPipelineEngine.process() → returns OPTIMIZED G-CODE
The route EXISTS. The pipeline EXISTS. The UI just calls the WRONG endpoint.

phases.title: Wire Pipeline to UI — Make Generate Post Actually Work

sessions.title: Connect Generate Post to Real Pipeline + Machine-Driven Stage Config

sessions.intent: User clicks Generate Post → gets real physics-optimized G-code formatted for their specific controller, not a hardcoded template. Every feature toggle maps to a pipeline stage.

units.title: Wire handleGenerate() to PostProcessorPipelineEngine via /ppg/generate route
units.description: In PostProcessorGeneratorPage.tsx: Change handleGenerate() to call the REAL pipeline endpoint (/ppg/generate or /ppg/optimize) instead of /ppg/template. Build PipelineInput from the UI state: (1) gcodeInput → input.gcode, (2) fingerprinted machine → input.machine (MachineContext), (3) selected controller → input.controller, (4) selected material (if available) → input.material. Keep the template endpoint as fallback if pipeline fails. The route /ppg/generate already maps to prism_cam post_process which invokes the pipeline.
exit_conditions: Test: Generate Post with Haas controller + real G-code → output has per-block S/F values (not template defaults)
Test: output_gcode contains G-code formatted in Haas dialect (G187, O-number format)
Test: stages array returned with Stage 1.1 base_speed_feed showing real kc1_1 value
Test: fallback to template if pipeline errors
abort_criteria: Output still returns hardcoded 164-line sample
Pipeline not actually invoked (check network tab)
No physics data in response (no stages, no forces)

units.title: Map feature toggles to pipeline StageConfig flags
units.description: Build a function mapFeaturesToStageConfig(selectedFeatures: string[], fingerprintResult: FingerprintResult): Partial<StageConfig> that maps: (1) 'probing_cycles' toggle → stages.probe_routines=true, (2) 'tsc' → stages.coolant_strategy=true + coolant.type='tsc', (3) 'high_speed_smoothing' → stages.toolpath_smoothing=true + motion_dynamics=true + look_ahead=true, (4) 'rtcp' → stages.multi_axis=true, (5) 'ssv' → stages.stability_rewrite=true, (6) 'subprograms' → stages.controller_features=true, (7) 'chip_conveyor' → stages.controller_features=true. Also map machine capabilities: fingerprint.max_rpm → machine.max_rpm, fingerprint.axis_count ��� machine.axes.
exit_conditions: Test: toggle HSM on → pipeline output includes Stage 3.1 toolpath_smoothing with status=pass
Test: toggle probing on → output includes Stage 6.2 probe_routines
Test: toggle SSV on → output includes Stage 3.4b stability_rpm_rewrite
Test: no toggles → pipeline still runs core physics (Stages 1.1, 2.1-2.7, 5.1, 6.1)
abort_criteria: Feature toggles don't change pipeline behavior
StageConfig not passed to pipeline input

units.title: Add material + tool selection to PPG page — auto S/F from user inputs
units.description: The PPG page has ZERO material or tool selection. Add: (1) Material picker: dropdown/search that queries MaterialRegistry (2,957 materials). Show ISO group badge (P/M/K/N/S/H) + kc1_1 value. Default options: common shop materials (4140, 6061, 304 SS, Ti-6Al-4V, D2, cast iron). Pass selected material as input.material to pipeline. (2) Tool entry: either manual (diameter, flute count, type dropdown matching ToolType enum: flat_endmill/ball/drill/tap/etc, material: carbide/HSS/ceramic/CBN) OR auto-extract from G-code (pipeline parseGCode already extracts T-numbers — enhance to pull diameter from tool change comments like '(TOOL - 10MM 4FL ENDMILL)'). (3) CAM tool import button: accept Fusion 360 .tools JSON or Mastercam .mcam-tools file → parse via FusionToolLibraryExtractorEngine → populate tool list. (4) When material+tool are set, pipeline Stage 1.1 computes Kienzle S/F automatically. Show 'Auto S/F: ON' badge when both are selected. Use lightsaber emerald-cyan border for this section.
exit_conditions: Test: select '4140 Steel' → pipeline input.material has kc1_1=2100, iso_group=P
Test: enter 10mm 4-flute carbide endmill → pipeline input.tools has diameter_mm=10, flute_count=4
Test: with material+tool selected, Generate → Stage 1.1 output has real computed S/F values
Test: S/F values match Kienzle: feed based on fz * z * n, speed from Taylor life target
Test: 'Auto S/F: ON' badge visible when both material and tool set
Test: tool type dropdown has all 12 ToolType values
Test: material picker shows ISO group color badge
abort_criteria: No material or tool selection on page
Material selected but not passed to pipeline input
Tool geometry not passed to pipeline (diameter missing)

units.title: Wire machine fingerprint into pipeline MachineContext + display physics results
units.description: (1) When MachinePickerPanel returns a FingerprintResult, build a full MachineContext from it (map manufacturer+model+year to max_rpm, max_power_kW, rapid_rate, axes, coolant_types, controller, etc). Store as resolved machine state. (2) In the pipeline output display, show the physics results: per-block force, power, tool life, wear, thermal. Add a 'Physics Summary' card (lightsaber emerald-cyan border) after the generated output showing: peak cutting force N, max power kW, estimated tool life min, safety score, stages that ran. (3) Show which PRISM advanced features were active in the output.
exit_conditions: Test: select 'Haas VF-2' → MachineContext has max_rpm=8100, max_power_kW=22.4, controller='haas'
Test: physics summary shows non-zero force, power, tool life values
Test: safety score displayed (0-1 from OmegaSafetyScoreEngine)
Test: 'PRISM Advanced Features' list shows which stages activated
abort_criteria: Physics summary shows all zeros or placeholder text
Machine fingerprint not forwarded to pipeline

sessions.title: Controller-Specific Output Formatting + Post Library as Pipeline Launcher

smart_config.role: CNC Post Processor Specialist + Controller Dialect Expert

knowledge: ControllerDialectEngine.ts — 25 dialects, ControllerFeatureSet, canned cycles, probing
AdvancedPostProcessorEngine.ts — enhance() with HSM, RTCP, tool management
PostLibraryUI.tsx — 13 templates, search, 'Generate for my machine' CTA
PostProcessorPipelineEngine.ts Stage 6.1 — G-code generation using dialect
sessions.intent: Haas users get Haas-specific G-code (G187, G234, O-numbers). Siemens users get Sinumerik (CYCLE800, TRAORI, COMPCAD). Each post library entry launches the pipeline pre-configured for that machine.

units.title: Ensure Stage 6.1 G-code output uses full ControllerDialect formatting
units.description: Verify and fix Stage 6.1 gcode_generation: (1) Output program uses dialect.program_start/program_end blocks. (2) Comments use dialect.comment_style (parentheses for Fanuc, semicolons for Siemens, block comments for Heidenhain). (3) Line numbers follow dialect.line_numbers style. (4) Canned cycles use dialect.canned_cycles mapping (G81→CYCLE81 for Siemens). (5) Arc format uses dialect.arc_format (IJK vs R-word). Verify for Haas, Fanuc, Siemens, Heidenhain, Mazak by running pipeline and checking output syntax.
exit_conditions: Test: Haas output starts with O-number, uses G187 for HSM, G81/G83 for drills
Test: Siemens output uses CYCLE81 not G81, COMPCAD not G187, semicolon comments
Test: Heidenhain output uses BEGIN PGM, CYCL DEF, block comments
Test: Fanuc output uses parenthesis comments, N-line numbers, G81 canned cycles
Test: all 5 controller outputs pass syntax validation against their dialect rules
abort_criteria: Output G-code is generic Fanuc regardless of controller selection
Dialect-specific codes (G187, CYCLE800, CYCL DEF) not present in output

units.title: Wire Stage 3.5 controller features: HSM, smoothing, TCPC, look-ahead per dialect
units.description: Verify Stage 3.5 controller_features injects the RIGHT codes per controller: (1) Haas: G187 P1/P2/P3 for smoothing levels, G234 for NURBS. (2) Siemens: CYCLE832 tolerance, COMPCAD, TRAORI for 5-axis. (3) Heidenhain: CYCL DEF 32 tolerance, M128 for TCPC. (4) Mazak: G05.1 Q1 for AI contour, G43.4 for TCPC. (5) Fanuc: G05.1 for AICC, G43.4/G43.5 for TCPC. Use ControllerDialectEngine.getDialect().features to get the codes. Ensure these appear in output G-code when corresponding feature toggle is active.
exit_conditions: Test: Haas + HSM toggle → output contains G187 P1 (rough) or G187 P3 (finish)
Test: Siemens + HSM → output contains CYCLE832(0.01) or COMPCAD
Test: Heidenhain + RTCP → output contains M128
Test: Mazak + HSM → output contains G05.1 Q1
Test: all feature codes match manufacturer documentation
abort_criteria: Feature codes hardcoded instead of sourced from ControllerDialectEngine
Wrong codes for controller (e.g., G187 emitted for Siemens)

units.title: Wire Post Library entries as pipeline launchers with pre-configured machine profiles
units.description: In PostLibraryUI: when user clicks a library entry (e.g., 'Haas NGC 3-Axis'), instead of showing a static template: (1) Pre-populate the PPG form with that machine's MachineContext (max_rpm, power, controller, features). (2) Auto-enable recommended features for that machine. (3) Set the pipeline to generate for that controller. (4) User just needs to paste/upload their G-code and click Generate. Each library entry maps to a real machine profile: {machine: MachineContext, recommended_features: string[], controller: ControllerFamily, description: string}.
exit_conditions: Test: click 'Haas NGC 3-Axis' → form populated with Haas VF-2 specs, probing+HSM recommended
Test: click 'Siemens 840D 5-Axis' → form populated with DMG DMU 50 specs, RTCP+HSM+probing recommended
Test: after library selection, user pastes G-code → Generate → gets real pipeline output for that machine
Test: library entries no longer show static template code
abort_criteria: Library still shows hardcoded template code
Library selection doesn't configure pipeline input

sessions.title: Advanced PRISM Features in Output + Size-Constrained vs Pipeline Modes

smart_config.role: CNC Manufacturing Intelligence Architect + Post Processor Expert

knowledge: AdvancedPostProcessorEngine.ts — enhance() with sister tooling, chip thinning, trochoidal
PostProcessorPipelineEngine.ts Stages 5.1/5.10 — safety gate + omega score
sessions.intent: Two output modes: (A) Self-contained post file with max features embedded in G-code comments/macros, or (B) Pipeline-optimized program where PRISM's full physics ran and the output has per-block optimized S/F. User understands what PRISM added to their program.

units.title: Add PRISM Advanced Feature injection into output G-code
units.description: After Stage 6.1 generates dialect-formatted G-code, inject PRISM advanced features as structured comments and inline annotations: (1) Per-block force comment: (PRISM: Fc=450N P=2.1kW T_life=18min) (2) Wear derating comment when applied: (PRISM: Wear VB=0.21mm → S derated 15%) (3) Chatter warning: (PRISM: RPM shifted from 6000→5400 — chatter avoidance) (4) Safety score in program header: (PRISM Safety Score: 0.87/1.00 — PASS) (5) Feature list in header: (PRISM Features: HSM G187, Kienzle S/F, Chatter RPM, Thermal Wear ODE) (6) Sustainability in footer: (PRISM LCA: 2.1 kgCO2, 0.8 kWh). These survive even if user strips PRISM branding — the physics is baked into the S/F values.
exit_conditions: Test: output header contains PRISM Safety Score line
Test: output header lists active PRISM features
Test: cutting blocks have force/power comments where physics ran
Test: comments use correct dialect comment syntax (parentheses for Fanuc, semicolons for Siemens)
Test: G-code is valid even if all PRISM comments are stripped
abort_criteria: Comments use wrong syntax for controller
Physics values in comments don't match actual S/F values in G-code
Comments break G-code parsing on real controllers

units.title: Implement dual output mode: self-contained post file vs pipeline-optimized program
units.description: Add output_mode to PipelineInput: 'self_contained' | 'pipeline_optimized'. (A) self_contained: output is a G-code file sized for controller memory (typically 100KB-10MB). Includes embedded parameter tables as macro variables where the controller supports them (Fanuc G65 P, Siemens R-params, Heidenhain Q-params). S/F values are inline constants. Good for shops without PRISM server access. (B) pipeline_optimized: output is full-detail G-code with PRISM annotations, physics comments, per-block optimization, sustainability data. Designed for PRISM-connected workflows where the server computes and the operator runs. UI shows toggle between modes with explanation.
exit_conditions: Test: self_contained mode → output has no PRISM server dependencies, runs standalone on controller
Test: pipeline_optimized mode → output has full PRISM annotations, per-block physics
Test: self_contained file size < 500KB for typical 1000-line program
Test: both modes produce valid G-code that passes syntax validation
abort_criteria: Self-contained mode still requires PRISM server to run
No way for user to choose between modes

units.title: Integration tests — real machines, real G-code, real physics assertions
units.description: Write end-to-end tests that simulate the full user flow: (1) Select Haas VF-2 → resolve fingerprint → set features → paste G-code → Generate → verify output is Haas dialect with physics-optimized S/F. (2) Same for Siemens 840D 5-axis. (3) Same for Fanuc Robodrill. (4) Same for Heidenhain TNC640. (5) Same for Mazak SmoothAi. Each test: verify correct dialect formatting, verify physics ran (forces > 0), verify safety score computed, verify feature codes present when toggled, verify output parses as valid G-code. (6) Test self_contained vs pipeline_optimized mode differences. Assert against canonical Kienzle forces for ISO P steel (kc1_1=1800).
exit_conditions: Test: >= 20 integration tests across 5 controller families
Test: ALL use real PostProcessorPipelineEngine.process() — zero mocks
Test: Haas output has O-number + G187 + parenthesis comments + Kienzle-computed feeds
Test: Siemens output has CYCLE81 + semicolons + COMPCAD + physics feeds
Test: Heidenhain output has BEGIN PGM + CYCL DEF + M128 + physics feeds
Test: Kienzle force for P-steel at ap=2mm fz=0.15mm within 20% of 1800*2*0.15^0.75
Test: safety score > 0 for all tests
Test: no NaN, no Infinity in any output
abort_criteria: ANY mock of PostProcessorPipelineEngine or ControllerDialectEngine
Tests that pass with || true or only check .toBeDefined()
Fewer than 20 tests
Missing any of the 5 controller families
